articles.description: A 37-year-old man, Biru Singh Bhadauriya, died after being assaulted in Kanpur's Hanumant Vihar area. The attack happened on Tuesday night when he was returning home from a Dussehra fair. His assailants allegedly trapped his hands in the car windows and dragged him for 1.5 kilometers. After the incident, Bhadauriya was taken to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital where he later died.

articles.title: Google co-founder Larry Page leaves California ahead of billionaire tax vote
articles.description: As Californians gear up to cast their votes on Proposition 40, which suggests a one-time tax on billionaires, notable figures like Larry Page have relocated their businesses far from the state's reach to evade this tax burden. While the tax could potentially rake in $100 billion, the exodus of these wealthy individuals—who would collectively owe around $29 billion—poses a serious threat to California's expected income from this tax initiative.

articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex tumbles 600 points, Nifty50 trades below 22,600
articles.full_text: Stock market today: Rupee offsets gains as Dalal Street struggles Asian equities struggled to sustain gains in early trade on Thursday as uncertainty surrounding the Gulf and concerns over artificial intelligence offset optimism around technology earnings. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.2%, putting it on track for a fourth consecutive weekly decline. Japan’s Nikkei gave up earlier gains to trade 0.4% lower, while South Korean shares fell more than 1%. In the broader regional market snapshot provided, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined 2.09%, South Korea’s Kospi fell 1.92% and Shenzhen lost 1.41%. Shanghai was down 0.69%, while Australia’s ASX 200 slipped 0.47%. The mixed-to-negative regional cues come as investors assess geopolitical risks and their potential implications for oil prices and global market sentiment. Oil prices rose on Thursday as fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the kingdom. Brent crude futures gained $1.29, or 1.2%, to $110.11 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 97 cents, or 1%, to $98.12. The latest escalation follows attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, including a strike at a civilian airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight, and a drone attack on an oil field that killed two people. Meanwhile, Iran’s foreign minister said the country was prepared to defend itself, while President Masoud Pezeshkian questioned the possibility of dialogue amid US pressure. The developments have added to uncertainty over regional security and energy supplies. Rupee strengthened 53 paise to close at 94.38 against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by foreign currency inflows linked to Reliance Industries’ Jio Platforms IPO and intervention by the Reserve Bank of India. The currency opened at 94.78, touched an intraday high of 94.35 and a low of 94.82 before settling at its strongest level in around six weeks. However, weak domestic equities and elevated crude oil prices continued to pose risks to the currency’s gains. Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, said the rupee could maintain a positive bias amid broad dollar weakness and softer US Treasury yields. The USD-INR spot rate is expected to trade in a range of Rs 94.20 to Rs 94.80, he said. Benchmark indices closed lower on Wednesday for a second consecutive session as selling in power, banking and financial stocks offset early gains. BSE Sensex declined 143.21 points, or 0.19%, to settle at 73,709.69, despite rising as much as 829.29 points to an intraday high of 74,682.19 before noon. Profit booking dragged the index more than 1,450 points from its high to a low of 73,229.45, before some late buying helped it recover. NSE Nifty50 fell 77.60 points, or 0.34%, to close at 22,811.35, after moving between 23,120.90 and 22,702.85. Midcap and smallcap indices also declined around 1.5% to 2.4%, reflecting broader risk aversion, according to Ajit Mishra, SVP–Research at Religare Broking.

articles.title: Big Tech in classrooms: Why parents should question Silicon Valley’s growing influence on education
articles.description: As technology companies expand their presence in classrooms, concerns are growing over their influence on curricula, teaching practices and student data. Drawing on technology reporter Natasha Singer’s book Coding Kids, the article examines how companies shape digital education and questions whether devices alone improve learning outcomes. It highlights the need for teacher support, thoughtful technology adoption and “tech civics,” encouraging students to understand technology’s power, accountability and social impact while helping parents and schools prioritise educational needs.

articles.description: DC Studios is set to release its first horror film titled 'Clayface' in theaters on October 23. Early viewers have praised the film for its body-horror sequences and Tom Rhys Harries' performance. However, some criticism has been directed toward the film's third act and tonal inconsistencies. 'Clayface' tells the tragic story of Matt Hagen, highlighting his transformation and descent into vengeance.
